text:
maria: FYI we saw sustained throttling in euw2 last night starting ~23:14 UTC, led to a near-OOM on a subset of model workers. Alert kicked from perf-bot.
aj: noticed long RT tails and batch sizes spiking. Routing started queueing and token latencies climbed.
liam: quick metrics dump — GPU mem hit ~94% on several nodes in pool inference-euw2-hot, batch size increased ~5x from baseline. Network egress to cache tier spiked ~3x.
sophia: autoscaler didn't react as expected; minReplicas was effectively pinned by the rollout policy we applied earlier. It blocked fast scale-up.
maria: logs show repeated gRPC reconnects to kv-cache; p99 KV latency jumped to ~350ms which caused workers to hold KV cache longer and increase per-request memory.
samir: timeline note — we had two spot drains in the AZ at 23:10 and 23:18 which removed ~20% of GPU capacity, compounding the issue.
aj: combine spot drains + pinned minReplicas + routing queue => scheduler condensed shards onto remaining GPUs -> memory pressure and swap-ish behavior.
liam: sample command we used: ```kubectl top pods -n inference | grep inference- | sort -k3 -nr``` gave the hot list; attaching snippet to retro doc.
sophia: cost discussion: removing preemptible/spot pools would reduce this risk but increase infra cost ~+30% monthly. Alternative: reserve a small dedicated buffer (10%) to absorb drains. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
maria: forecasting problem: our seasonal model underpredicted the promo spike by ~28% in GPU hours. We need a tail-focused scenario in forecasting (99th pct demand).
aj: immediate lessons: 1) routing should detect KV latency and failover to healthy cache replicas or bypass cache for critical short-path requests; 2) autoscaler policy must allow emergency burst ups even when pinned; 3) faster handling for spot drains (auto-fill with warm dedicated nodes).
liam: proposed actions: @liam - add routing cold-path to failover to alternate cache replica (ETA: Mon), @sophia - run cost/benefit for 10% dedicated cushion and share numbers (ETA: Thu), @aj - change autoscaler to allow emergency_scale flag and run backtest (ETA: Tue), @maria - add KV tail latency alert and dashboard panel (done), @samir - draft incident timeline and retro (ETA: Wed).
ops-bot: Incident mitigation applied at 23:44 UTC: shed low-priority background requests, cold-started 4 dedicated nodes, and routing temporarily limited batch sizes to steady queues. Post-mitigation p95 latency returned to baseline by 00:12 UTC.
samir: I'll start the writeup and include raw graphs + the kube top snippets. Will share in #incidents-retrospectives.
maria: extra follow-up: consider model-variant fallback (quantized/less-KV variant) as a graceful degradation path when mem pressure is high.
aj: noted — will prototype a variant-fallback policy in the routing layer.
liam: thanks everyone. I'll open the PR for routing failover and link to the retro doc. Closing thread here.
